guideLink: Rules are written in Elo. <link>Writing a rule</link> explains how, with rules to start from.
guideMore: Writing a rule: the guide, with rules to start from
guideIntro: A rule is one expression, written in Elo. It is given an email and answers one of the attribute’s values, or null to say nothing. It runs on this server when an email is fetched: no AI, no cost.
eloSite: The whole language, with a place to try expressions: elo-lang.org
fieldsPick: The email, as _. Click a field to write it in the rule.
fieldsIntro: The email, as _: each field with its type.

field.fromAddress: The address of who sent it
field.fromName: The name of who sent it
field.subject: Its subject
field.attachments: Its attachments: name, kind, size in bytes
field.mailbox: The address of the mailbox it arrived in
field.answered: Whether the mailbox marks it as answered
field.precedence: bulk, junk or list for mass mail

brief.naming: Name a part, use it after “in”.
brief.contains: A text holds another, whatever its case.
brief.any: True when one item of a list fits.
brief.chain: A chain: each step is given the one before.

skillTitle: Have an AI assistant write it
skillGeneral: This skill teaches an AI assistant what a rule is given, what it must answer, and enough of Elo to write one. Each attribute also offers its own, which names it and its values. What the assistant writes is pasted in the editor and tried like any rule.
triedTitle: {count, plural, =0 {No recent email to try it on} one {On your most recent email} other {On your # most recent emails}} · nothing was changed
triedShares: How many emails get each value
shapeGiven: A rule is given the email as _: who sent it, its subject, its text, its attachments, the mailbox it arrived in, a few headers.
shapeAnswers: It answers a value of the attribute, by its name ('billing'), or null to say nothing. To say why, it answers '{'value: …, reason: …'}': the reason is shown with the value on the email.
shapeNothing: When a rule says nothing, the email keeps no value for that attribute, unless the attribute also asks the AI. A value a member set by hand is never replaced by a rule.

recipe.domainWhat: Everything from one client is high priority.
recipe.words: By words in the subject or the text
recipe.wordsWhat: A topic from a few keywords, in two languages.
recipe.mailbox: By the mailbox it arrived in
recipe.mailboxWhat: What reaches the billing address is billing.
recipe.reasonWhat: The reason is shown with the value on the email.

checkedType: As you write, the rule is checked against the type of the email: a field an email does not have, or a text used as a number, is shown where it is, and the rule cannot be saved.
checkedLimits: A rule may take a tenth of a second on an email, and be 4,000 characters long.
checkedValues: An answer that is not one of the attribute’s values counts as saying nothing.
checkedFails: A rule that fails on an email says nothing of it: the email is fetched all the same.
